## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads.

## Cache saturation
All measured N values exceed the L1d spill (N≈963); N=10000 is L2-resident while N≥100000 crosses the L2 spill (N≈61680). At q=0.01, cost FALLS from 8.779 ns/p (N=10000, L2-resident) to 7.996 (N=100000, DRAM), reflecting overhead amortization that outweighs the spill penalty, then rises gently to 8.23 at N=10000000 — no sharp L2→DRAM knee. Death rate raises the floor without altering the N-shape: at q=0.5 the curve is flat at 13.253–13.383 ns/p for N≤100000 then drifts to 14.092 at N=10000000, preserving the same gentle-rise form but shifted up by ~5 ns/p.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved bandwidth is 8.5 GB/s at N=100000, q=0.01 — 28% of the 29.9 GB/s streaming ceiling. The algo is compute-bound at low death rates (compute=65.7%, backend_stall=29.6% at N=100000, q=0.01) and transitions to branch-bound as q rises: at q=0.5, branch_flush reaches 35.7% and bandwidth falls to 5.13 GB/s (17% of ceiling). It never becomes bandwidth-bound at any measured regime; the gap to ceiling widens with death rate as branchy respawn cost dominates.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized component-wise within a single particle, not across particles. The math loop (0x10004da4c–0x10004daa4) uses `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s` on four floats and `fmul.2s`/`fadd.2s` on two, with `ext.16b` and `mov.s v17[3], v6[0]` to rearrange components, plus an indexed gather `ld1.s {v16}[1], [x10]`. Stride is 0x44 (68 bytes) per particle. The decide/respawn loops are entirely scalar with `ldrb`/`strb` byte-granular scatter stores (19 strb in the histogram). This component-wise vec on stride-68 explains why bandwidth stays at 28% of ceiling — each iteration touches one particle's 68 bytes without cross-particle streaming — and the byte stores in loop2 cap it further.

## Verdict
Refuted — at q=0.01 the algo achieves only 8.5 GB/s = 28% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling, with compute at 65.7% confirming it is compute-bound, not bandwidth-bound. The component-wise `fmul.4s` auto-vec operates within one particle's 68-byte stride, not across particles, so it cannot approach streaming. At q=0.5, branch_flush rises to 35.7% and bandwidth drops to 5.13 GB/s, confirming the non-Halide-expressible loop2 dominates under churn.
